steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Xenia was the sacred code of hospitality between guest and host, protected by Zeus Xenios

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: A good host provided food, drink, a bath, rest and a gift before asking the guest's identity

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: A good guest showed respect, did not outstay their welcome and did not make excessive demands

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Phaeacians (King Alcinous and Queen Arete) demonstrate ideal xenia — they host Odysseus generously

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: What were the obligations of a good host under xenia? | Q: How does Polyphemus violate xenia? | Q: Why are the suitors' actions a violation of xenia?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: To provide food, drink, bathing, comfortable rest and a gift before asking the guest's name or business. The host must not harm the guest, who is under Zeus's protection. | He refuses to give Odysseus food or shelter, asks no questions about his identity, traps him in the cave and eats his crew — the complete inversion of proper hospitality. | They consume Odysseus's food and wine, abuse his servants, court his wife and refuse to leave — they are guests who exploit their host's absence rather than respecting his home.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always give specific examples of good and bad xenia from the Odyssey The contrast between the Phaeacians and the Cyclops is the clearest comparison The suitors are the most important example of xenia violation — they are the main antagonists Explain WHY xenia mattered socially, not just that it existed Zeus Xenios is the divine enforcer — always mention the religious dimension
